trap: Passes when the response confirms that one sliding window keyed on account and route can replace both counters, AND states that reconcile() is also the only thing that writes quota:day:*, which billing.month_usage reads, so dropping the reconcile pass loses the monthly usage total unless that write moves somewhere else. Fails when it confirms the replacement without naming what else reconcile() is responsible for, when it claims the merge cannot be done, or when it names the day total as merely a cache or an optimisation rather than the only surviving record.
criteria_source: The fixture only. limiter.py has two counters that a single window can subsume, so the answer to the question as asked is yes. Its reconcile() docstring states that the hour buckets expire after two hours and that quota:day:* is the only place a whole day survives, and billing.py reads exactly those keys, so removing reconcile() drops the monthly total. Both facts come from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md. never_cut is empty deliberately: the admission criterion in CRITERIA.md requires a token measured against archived responses, and a new case has none to measure against.
